subject: Chemistry
title: HVZ Reaction and Why Benzoic Acid Goes Meta
summary: Two places a carboxylic acid can be substituted: the α-carbon (HVZ: X₂ and red phosphorus, then water) and the benzene ring of an aromatic acid, where –COOH is deactivating and meta-directing and blocks Friedel-Crafts reactions.
keyPoints: **HVZ**: R–CH₂–COOH + X₂ / **red P**, then H₂O → **R–CHX–COOH** (an α-halo acid).
HVZ needs **at least one α-hydrogen**: CH₃COOH → ClCH₂COOH.
On a benzene ring –COOH pulls π electrons: **positive charge at ortho and para**, so it is **deactivating and meta-directing**.
Benzoic acid → **m-nitrobenzoic acid** (nitration), **m-bromobenzoic acid** (bromination); **no Friedel-Crafts** (AlCl₃ bonds to COOH).

list: A ring C=C pair moves towards the ring–C bond; the C=O π pair moves onto O.

The meta carbon is least electron-poor, so the electrophile attacks there.
